Solid gameplay, a haunting atmosphere, and a great soundtrack. There are plenty of items to find/collect providing some replay value and the game looks good even on medium and lower graphics settings. Now if only they could have tied it all together with a decent story....

You have some ability to roam and make decisions, but for the most part the story is linear and kind of let down. Especially since every one of the reviews I read prior to buying said it was great. The game excels at creating atmospheric suspense, but also relies heavily on jump scares which come off as rather gimmicky after a while.

I spent a good 14 hours the first time through and still didn't find everything I was trying to, but the storyline itself amounted to maybe 9 or 10 hours. A more serious player can probably get through normal mode in less than 8 hours.

It's a good game, but it could have been great if the writers had tried just a wee bit harder. You'll know what I mean after you play through it. I think $60 is a little much for this one, but that's the norm now so I guess you just have to deal with it or a wait a while for it go on sale.

After the atrocious Resident Evil 6, Capcom reinvents itself to offer a more horror oriented entry of Resident Evil from the perspective of a common civilian in search of his wife who went missing in Louisiana: Ethan Winters. Since you no longer control an action hero like Leon, Chris, Jill, or Ada, this game feels more personal, and the first person perspective increases the creepyness of the Baker's House. The intro itself already sets the tone of the game, although its very tedious to get through on subsequent playthroughs because its very linear and has a lot of cutscenes. This fact also impacts replayability in a negative way, but playing on harder difficulties also changes a few things like puzzles. items and enemy placement.

This changes once the game lets you explore the Baker's house, because it's reminiscent of the Spencer Mansion from RE1, where you have to solve intricate puzzles (which are canonically made by the same people who worked for Spencer, a fun detail) and you feel there is danger at every corner for the entire game except the endgame, which is more linear and the setting changes to a bit more action-oriented. 

Overall, I think Capcom did the right choice by returning to survival horror instead of action-horror, because this game literally revived the franchise, and just for that i'm gonna give it a 9/10. It also was the introduction of their new RE Engine which would be used for all subsequent games and remakes.

Can't believe i waited so long to play this. Grim visuals, horrifying antagonists, a decent story and a gratifying mix of tense action and survival mechanics, with the occasional breezy puzzle thrown in, all combine to make this a top shelf addition to the Resident Evil franchise.

Resident Evil 7 was honestly one of the most intense survival horror experiences I've played. The first-person perspective made everything feel more terrifying, especially when exploring the Baker family house. Every dark hallway, strange noise, and unexpected encounter kept me on edge.

What I enjoyed the most was the atmosphere. The game constantly made me feel unsafe, even when nothing was happening. The Baker family was easily one of the highlights, especially Jack Baker, who made every encounter stressful and unpredictable. I also loved how the game brought back the classic survival horror elements, such as limited ammunition, inventory management, exploration, and puzzles.

However, I felt the game lost some of its momentum toward the end. The later sections weren't as scary or engaging as the beginning, and the lack of enemy variety made certain encounters feel repetitive.

Overall, I really enjoyed Resident Evil 7. It successfully brought back the fear and tension that made the earlier Resident Evil games so memorable. Despite its flaws, it's still an unforgettable horror experience that I would definitely recommend to anyone who loves survival horror.

A breath of fresh air for Resident Evil franchise

Resident Evil 7 reminds me a lot of Resident Evil 4. Although these games are very different at their cores, both of them were pioneers of change RE franchise desperately needed and set a trend that lasted for many games to come. Unsurprisingly, both of these games are my favourites in the series.

RE 7 decided to take vastly different approach from RE6 - gone are the Michael Bay-esque explosions and never ending action - all of that had been replaced by ominous atmosphere, slow and methodical gameplay and intricate, slowly unraveling story. Developers really tried to make every single aspect of the game polished to perfection and I believe that apart from few scratches, they succeeded. RE 7 is a must-play for both fans of all games in RE franchise as well as for newcomers.

Pros
+ Incredible visual presentation - RE engine simply looks awesome
+ Astounding sound design
+ OST
+ Gameplay with seamless transitions into cutscenes
+ Cutscenes and voice-acting along with acting performances are top-notch
+ Main story
+ Length of twice the amount of other similar horror games
+ Animations
+ Lighting
+ Season pass is one of the better ones

Cons:
- Choice of ending does not really matter
- Few bugs
- Enemy variety is really low

Gameplay:
Good, though seemingly inconsistent enemy health.
Survival horror mechanics are well applied, choice between health or ammo really makes your moment to moment decisions tense. Bosses can be a bit tedious; large healthbars, slow reloads and player uncertainty of how they're actually supposed to beat them. Multiple endings and collectables with bonus difficulties help with replay-ability.

Story (minimal spoilers):
Pretty standard modern horror. Tired "evil child" cliche. Overall well paced and doesn't drag on. Majority of "scares" come from gross out body horror however the game's sound design makes for some great atmosphere.
